article.title: Nithya Raman Replaces Karen Bass
article.author: Dick Platkin
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. LA has a new Mayor. But if you now expect major changes from her, let me set you straight. The new mayor, Nithya Raman, may have a different personality, age, and separate supporters from the defeated mayor, Karen Bass, but they have much more in common than their differences. And if you think that things in Los Angeles will be substantially different under the new mayor, it is time for you to reconsider. The County is still losing 54,000 people per year and the City of Los Angeles, 5,000 to 10,000 residents per year. The missing people left the Los Angeles region for nearby cheaper areas or for other states, like Nevada or Texas. They are not coming back. Nevertheless, we are told by the “experts” that we still suffer from a housing shortage. The thousands of vacant units are supposedly not suitable for those in desperate need of housing, the homeless and overcrowded. In fact, the Los Angeles area suffers from both vacant housing and people who live in overcrowded conditions because they can’t afford a vacant apartment or house to move in to. As for new housing, the homeless and overcrowded are both priced out. Related: Over-crowded Homes in LA County and How to Help Them Why is the LA region stuck in this rut? The basic answer is that so many people are low income that they cannot afford existing, vacant housing. Landlords choose to keep their units empty rather than lowering the rent, so the homeless and overcrowded cannot afford them. It is easy to understand why the units still sit empty, but harder to fathom why so many working people cannot afford a permanent and appropriate place to live in Los Angeles, the country’s second largest city. The main explanation for why there are so many homeless and overcrowded people in the Los Angeles area, and why they cannot afford to live in an apartment or house is financial . They can’t afford to buy, and they can’t afford to rent, even though many of them hold a fulltime job. They sleep in their cars or in nonresidential structures, such as garages. They pray they don’t get caught or have any unexcepted expenses. Related: Living in Cars: LA's Hidden Homelessness Crisis Life on the margin. We don’t know how many people fall into these categories, but we know that there are over 1,000,000 people living in overcrowded conditions in LA County, as shown on this map. The bulk of them are in the South Central area, but also in Burbank, Long Beach, and Alhambra. Overcrowded housing in Los Angeles County. If LA’s new mayor, Nithia Raman, can truly tackle homelessness and overcrowded, she will have sufficiently separated herself from her predecessor, defeated Mayor Karen Bass, to warrant serious praise. Until then she will be remembered for her similarities, not differences, with her defeated opponent. So far Nithia Raman’s reputation is based on her successful campaign to become LA’s next Mayor, not for solving LA’s closely related problems of homelessness and overcrowding. If her administration can somehow solve these two citywide housing problems, then she will have something to boast about. If not, as I predict, then she can only brag about her successful campaign to unseat LA’s outgoing mayor, Karen Bass.
